messages.subject: Dropping Individuals & Fixing A<>B mis-coding
parts:
Karl:  

Two questions:

1.  If, after loading data into R/qtl, you find that you need to drop (delete) some individuals from your populations.  What, then, is the R/qtl best command set for doing that?

2.  If, after finding a couple of markers with switched A<>B coding, what simple command have you used for letter-coded genotyping?  The solution offered on page 55 of the Broman & Sen book for inverting numerically-coded genotypes of 1,2,3,- is clever, i.e.,  g[,"c1m3"] < 4 - g[,"c1m3"], but I am having a brain-block today relative to devising an equally clever R command (too little experience with R, I guess) for inverting letter-coded F2 genotypes of A,H,B,-.  

Your e-mailed help on these two questions would be greatly appreciated.  

- Jim

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Dropping Individuals & Fixing A<>B mis-coding
parts: > 1.  If, after loading data into R/qtl, you find that you need to drop (delete) some individuals from your populations.  What, then, is the R/qtl best command set for doing that?

There's a function subset.cross that you can use to select a portion of individuals or a portion of chromosomes. Do something like the following (for the case that there's a phenotype column "id" that specifies individuals.

ind2drop <- c("A123", "A135", "A380", "A544", "A865", "A928")
mycross <- subset(mycross, ind=is.na(match(ind2drop, mycross$pheno$id)))

> 2. If, after finding a couple of markers with switched A<>B coding, what simple command have you used for letter-coded genotyping? The solution offered on page 55 of the Broman & Sen book for inverting numerically-coded genotypes of 1,2,3,- is clever, i.e., g[,"c1m3"] < 4 - g[,"c1m3"], but I am having a brain-block today relative to devising an equally clever R command (too little experience with R, I guess) for inverting letter-coded F2 genotypes of A,H,B,-.

The genotype codes become 1, 2, 3, once the data are loaded into R, and so "4 - genotype" replaces 1,2,3 with 3,2,1, since 4-1=3, 4-2=2 and 4-3=1.

In the development version of R/qtl (available at http://www.rqtl.org/download), there's a function switchAlleles() to do this. I wish I'd thought of it before the book was published.

mycross <- switchAlleles(mycross, "amarkername")

karl
